findings.summary: The page titled "IAM Policies / Policies and Permissions" contains almost no policy content — after two stranded IAM bullets it is entirely EC2 material, while the EC2 definition that should open it is marooned at the bottom of the IAM page.
findings.evidence: Page 2 ends with "EC2 provides ==resizable compute capacity==; launch virtual servers (instances) and run applications."; page 3 (`page_title":"IAM Policies"`, `hero":"iam"`, `subtitle":"Policies and Permissions"`) then runs "1. Key Concepts" → cards "AMI / Pre-configured template to launch an instance", "Instance Types / t2.micro, m5.large, c6i.large", "2. Instance Lifecycle", "3. Pricing Options".
findings.fix: Move the trailing EC2 paragraph from page 2 to the top of page 3, retitle page 3 "EC2 - Compute" with `hero: "ec2"` and subtitle "Elastic Compute Cloud", and move its two opening IAM bullets ("Roles give ==temporary credentials==…", "Resources identified by ARN…") up beside the policy code block in page 2's section 6.

findings.summary: The VPC Peering section claims peering works with overlapping CIDR blocks, which AWS explicitly forbids.
findings.evidence: "Supports overlapping CIDR with caution"
findings.fix: Replace with "VPCs must have non-overlapping CIDRs — a peering request between VPCs with matching or overlapping IPv4/IPv6 CIDRs fails; use PrivateLink or a private NAT gateway + Transit Gateway for overlapping ranges."

findings.summary: A networking comparison table ("10. NACL vs SG") is spliced into the middle of the storage sequence, between sections 2 and 3.
findings.evidence: Page 9 heading order is "2. S3" → "10. NACL vs SG" (table Type/Level/Rule for NACL vs SG) → "3. EFS" → "4. FSx" → "5. S3 Storage Classes".
findings.fix: Move the "10. NACL vs SG" heading and table to the end of page 8, after "9. Traffic Flow", so the storage page reads 1→8 uninterrupted.

findings.summary: The sample IAM policy pairs the bucket-level action s3:ListBucket with an object-level ARN, so the policy grants no listing permission at all.
findings.evidence: "Action": ["s3:ListBucket"], "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/*"]
findings.fix: Change the Resource to the bucket ARN "arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket" (use "arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/*" only for object actions such as s3:GetObject) — matching the correct example already used on page 10.

findings.summary: SMS is listed as a current IAM MFA option, but AWS ended support for enabling SMS text-message MFA for IAM users.
findings.evidence: "SMS MFA"
findings.fix: Remove the SMS MFA bullet and replace it with "Passkey / FIDO security key (phishing-resistant, AWS-recommended)".

findings.summary: The Security Groups recap says security groups have deny rules, which they do not (allow-only), and it contradicts the document's own tables on pages 7 and 9.

findings.summary: The One Zone-IA card implies data is recreated after an AZ loss, when in fact the data is not resilient to AZ loss and the customer must be able to recreate it.
findings.evidence: {"title":"One Zone-IA","text":"Single AZ, recreated if AZ destroyed"}
findings.fix: Change to "Single AZ; data is lost if that AZ is destroyed — use only for data you can recreate".
